t71iii_tf89c: Being the grown-up doesn't mean your little one has to leave the room. t71iii_tf11b: Intuition is great at catching a pattern before you can explain it. Checking is a different job: does it contradict itself, how has it done before, does the conclusion actually follow? And the part of you that does the checking can get tired of not knowing, and be pretty relieved to hand the job off, to a hunch or to somebody else. I wouldn't let either one take over. A strong intuitive click is real information, and it still has to check out.
t71iii_tf11c: A hunch can be onto something before you can say why, since it can pick up on a pattern before your head has the words for it. Then let your head check it, for holes in the story and for how hunches like it have done before. Does the conclusion follow from it? Watch for getting tired of not knowing, too, because it can be a relief to hand the whole question over to a hunch, or to somebody else. I wouldn't let either one run the show alone. A really strong click is still just something to weigh.
